title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
This is a detection and response failure inside an autonomous driving system, not a mechanical one. The vehicle was operating in autonomous mode on a public residential street with a human safety operator present, and it struck a duck without slowing or stopping. The object in its path was small, low to the ground, and outside the roadway, which places the failure at the perception stage of the stack rather than in steering or braking.

Catching it would have required either a perception system that classified a small animal near the curb as an obstacle warranting a stop, or a safety operator who intervened before contact. The reports do not establish what the operator did or did not do in the moments before the collision, and the operator's presence alone did not prevent it.

What is not established is the residents' claim that the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, which Avride disputed, and that remains an allegation rather than a finding. The reports also do not establish intent, a defect determination, or any regulatory conclusion about the vehicle or the company.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, which made residents particularly upset about the incident. A local resident posted about the event on a neighborhood Facebook group, and some residents claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim.

In response to the controversy, Avride adjusted its testing operations by restricting the autonomous vehicle from certain streets around the lake where the incident occurred. The company reviewed vehicle data and has launched controlled simulation experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations. Additionally, community members have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Avride stated it will continue testing on public roads overall, while other companies including Zoox, Tesla, and Waymo also operate autonomous vehicles in Austin.
